items.content:
테슬라와 스페이스X의 합병이 본격적으로 논의 되고 있습니다. 두 회사는 각각 독립 이사들로 구성된 특별위원회를 설치했으며, 일론 머스크 CEO도 합병에 상당한 장점이 있다고 밝혔습니다. 양사의 기업가치를 합치면 3조5000억달러(약 4634조원)에 달하는 초대형 기업이 탄생하게 됩니다. 월가에서는 합병을 기정사실로 보는 분위기지만, 정작 합병 가격을 놓고는 의견이 엇갈리고 있습니다. 테슬라 주주들에게 얼마나 많은 대가를 지급할 것인지, 머스크의 지배력이 얼마나 커질 것인지가 주요 쟁점 입니다.

하지만 AI 산업의 관점에서 보면 이번 합병은 조금 다른 의미가 있습니다. 두 회사가 합쳐지면 단순히 세계 최대 규모의 기업이 등장하는 것뿐만 아니라, AI 모델 개발부터 자동차와 로봇, 반도체와 데이터센터, 통신망까지 갖춘 거대한 AI 기업이 탄생하기 때문입니다.

지금까지 첨단 AI 경쟁은 주로 디지털 환경을 중심으로 전개됐습니다. 오픈AI와 앤트로픽은 챗봇과 코딩 에이전트, 기업용 업무 자동화에 집중해 왔습니다. 구글과 아마존, 메타는 자체 서비스와 인프라를 갖고 있지만, 주요 AI 서비스는 여전히 디지털 환경에 기반을 두고 있습니다. 테슬라와 스페이스X가 합쳐진다면 자동차와 로봇이라는 물리적 제품이 AI 사업의 중심에 놓인다는 점에서 차이가 있습니다.

지난 1~2년 사이 두 회사의 사업 성격도 크게 달라졌습니다. 테슬라는 전기자동차 제조사에서 자율주행과 로봇을 핵심 성장 사업으로 내세우는 기업으로 바뀌고 있습니다. 2024년 공개한 무인 자율주행차 '사이버캡'에 이어 최근에는 휴머노이드 로봇 '옵티머스'의 초기 생산도 시작했습니다. 스페이스X도 로켓과 위성통신 사업에 머물지 않습니다. xAI를 흡수한 뒤 AI 모델과 컴퓨팅 사업을 크게 키웠으며, 지난 3분기에는 전체 매출 146억달러 중 AI 모델과 컴퓨팅 등을 포함한 사업 매출이 76억달러로 절반을 넘었습니다. 이제 두 회사 모두 AI가 사업의 중심으로 들어온 셈입니다.

합병 이후 가장 큰 경쟁력으로 예상되는 것은 피지컬 AI 개발에 필요한 방대한 실사용 데이터와 이를 직접 확보할 수 있는 환경입니다. 현재 피지컬 AI 개발의 가장 큰 병목 중 하나는 데이터 수집입니다. 언어 모델은 인터넷에서 수집한 텍스트와 코드 등으로 학습할 수 있지만, 로봇은 실제 공간에서 움직이고 물체를 다루는 과정에서 발생하는 데이터를 확보해야 합니다. 이를 위해 별도의 실험 시설을 만들거나 외부 기업과 협력해야 하는 AI 개발사들과 달리, 테슬라는 이미 자동차와 공장이라는 대규모 실사용 환경을 갖추고 있습니다.

차량의 실제 주행 데이터를 분석해 자율주행 시스템을 개선하고 있으며, 앞으로 공장에 옵티머스를 본격 투입하면 로봇 학습에 필요한 작업 데이터도 직접 확보할 수 있습니다. 향후 로봇이 대량 보급되면 데이터 확보 규모도 크게 늘어날 수 있습니다. 모델 개발과 데이터 수집, 실제 제품에서의 검증을 자체적으로 수행할 수 있다는 점은 피지컬 AI 경쟁에서 상당한 우위로 이어질 가능성이 있습니다. 다만 자동차 주행 데이터와 로봇의 작업 데이터는 성격이 다르며, 옵티머스는 이제 초기 생산 단계라는 점에서 실제 데이터 확보 규모는 아직 지켜봐야 합니다.

최근 공개된 ' 그록 보이스 3.0 '은 AI 모델과 자체 서비스의 결합을 보여주는 사례입니다. 지난 14일 공개된 이 모델은 아티피셜 애널리시스의 음성 AI 평가에서 86.9점으로 1위를 기록했습니다. 현재 테슬라 차량에서 하루 수백만건의 대화를 처리하고 있으며, 스타링크 고객센터에서도 하루 2만건의 통화에 사용되고 있습니다. 회사에 따르면 고객센터 통화의 약 70%를 사람의 개입 없이 처리한다고 합니다. 자체 개발한 모델을 계열사의 자동차와 통신 서비스에 곧바로 적용하고 있는 것입니다.

실제 서비스에서 발생하는 문제와 고객의 요구를 모델 개선에 반영할 기회도 확보할 수 있습니다. 다만 이러한 실사용 데이터가 그록 보이스의 성능 향상에 얼마나 기여했는지는 공개되지 않았습니다.

또 다른 경쟁력은 AI를 작동시키는 기반 시설입니다. 스페이스X는 지난 3분기 말 기준 1.7기가와트(GW) 규모의 AI 연산 인프라를 확보했으며, 스타링크 위성망을 운영하고 있습니다.

여기에 테슬라의 배터리와 에너지 저장장치, 자체 AI 반도체 설계 능력이 더해집니다. 두 회사는 이미 대규모 반도체 생산시설인 '테라팹'을 공동 추진하고 있으며, 스페이스X는 우주 데이터센터 사업도 구상하고 있습니다. AI 모델을 학습할 데이터센터와 반도체, 전력 공급 장치, 제품을 연결할 통신망까지 직접 확보하려는 것입니다. 테라팹과 우주 데이터센터의 사업성은 아직 검증되지 않았지만, AI 경쟁에서 연산 자원과 전력, 통신망의 중요성이 커지고 있다는 점에서 의미가 있습니다.

사업 구조도 주목됩니다. 오픈AI와 앤트로픽은 주로 외부 기업과 개인에게 AI 모델과 서비스를 판매합니다. 테슬라와 스페이스X가 합쳐진 기업은 모델을 외부에 판매하는 동시에 자율주행 소프트웨어와 자동차 음성 서비스, 스타링크 고객지원, 향후 옵티머스까지 자사 제품과 서비스에 직접 활용할 수 있습니다.

물론 구글도 검색과 안드로이드, 웨이모를 갖고 있으며, 아마존도 클라우드와 물류 로봇을 운영하고 있습니다. 하지만 자동차와 휴머노이드 로봇, 위성통신, AI 컴퓨팅과 반도체 사업을 한꺼번에 결합한다는 점은 차별적입니다. 특히 AI가 소프트웨어를 넘어 현실 세계의 기계와 설비를 움직이는 기술로 발전할수록 이런 사업들의 연결 가능성은 커질 수 있습니다.

그렇다고 합병이 곧바로 압도적인 AI 경쟁력으로 이어진다는 뜻은 아닙니다. 두 회사는 이미 독립적인 기업으로 운영되면서도 그록의 차량 탑재와 테라팹 개발 등에서 협력하고 있습니다. 기술적 시너지를 얻기 위해 반드시 법적으로 하나의 기업이 돼야 하는 것은 아닙니다.

합병에 따른 지배구조 문제와 막대한 투자 부담도 남아 있습니다. 특히 머스크가 스페이스X에서 보유한 의결권은 약 85%인 데 비해 테슬라에서는 약 20%로 차이가 커 합병 조건을 둘러싼 논쟁도 불가피합니다.

이번 합병 논의는 AI 산업에서 실사용 환경과 데이터 확보 능력이 얼마나 중요한 경쟁력이 될 수 있을지 가늠해 보는 기회이기도 합니다. 테슬라와 스페이스X가 실제로 합쳐질지는 아직 알 수 없지만, AI 경쟁의 무대가 디지털에서 현실 세계로 넓어지는 과정에서 두 회사가 어떤 역할을 할지 지켜볼 만합니다.

■ 딥시크, AI 운영 비용 낮출 핵심 추론 기술 '딥인퍼' 오픈소스 공개

딥시크가 기존에는 AI 모델을 공개하는 데 집중했다면, 이번에는 실제 서비스에서 모델을 구동하고 연산 자원을 관리하는 서빙 엔진까지 공개했습니다. 자사의 저비용·고효율 AI 운영 방식도 외부 개발자들이 활용할 수 있도록 했습니다.

알트먼은 AI 개발 속도 조절 방안을 논의하면서 한 기업이 AGI를 독점하기 위해 경쟁사의 GPU까지 파괴하는 극단적인 시나리오를 소개하고, 이를 "끔찍하다"고 평가했습니다. 다리오 아모데이도 AI 기술이 소수 기업에 집중되는 상황을 경계해 왔다는 점에서, 기술 독점의 위험성에는 공통된 인식을 갖고 있다는 사실이 드러납니다.

가트너의 2027년 10대 전략기술에 대형양적모델과 음성 추론 모델, 월드 모델 등이 포함된 것은 AI 기술의 중심이 언어 모델을 넘어 다양한 모델과 산업 응용 분야로 넓어지고 있음을 보여줍니다. 또 AI가 소프트웨어를 개발하는 속도가 사람의 검토 능력을 앞지르고 에이전트의 자율성이 높아지는 만큼, AI 시스템의 권한과 보안, 운영 구조를 직접 관리해야 한다고 강조했습니다.

Turning Database Grading into RL Rewards: Post-Training Agents with ThinkingBox
items.content:
This is the follow up to our first blog post, The Agent Said It Was Done. The Database Disagreed. ThinkingBox-Training is now available on GitHub .

We built ThinkingBox to evaluate an agent's work by comparing the final database state with the expected outcome. We then used the same kind of executable signal as a reward on training tasks outside ThinkingBox-Bench. For Qwen3.8-27B, average success rose from 51.70% to 60.78%, while tasks completed correctly on all twenty attempts rose from 38 to 107 with 50 GRPO steps.

Figure 1. ThinkingBox turns executable checks of terminal database state into rewards for post-training agents on tasks outside ThinkingBox-Bench.

We built ThinkingBox to catch agents that say they are done when they are not.

Each of its 507 tasks in ThinkingBox-Bench (our benchmark dataset) hands an agent a real backend and a set of tools, lets it work, then checks what really changed in the database. In the first post , we caught a model closing a customer's ticket as resolved while the carrier exception behind it was still open. Nine competent-looking tool calls, one wrong database row.

Then we noticed what we had built. For most tasks, an executable check can return 1 or 0 directly from the final database state. That is not just a grader. This can be a reward function. +

So we constructed a training pool from ThinkingBox-format tasks outside the benchmark and used their executable outcomes as rewards. The catch was choosing which tasks are suitable for agent training: most tasks are either already solved or hopeless for the model in front of you, and both teach it nothing.

Difficulty is policy-relative: a task is hard for the current model only until that model learns it.

We call this offline policy-relative difficulty . We estimated each task's success probability once using the base policy before training and kept the selected training pool fixed throughout the run.

We used offline policy-relative difficulty to build the training pool, then fine-tuned Qwen3.8-27B with GRPO for 50 steps. To recap, we evaluate each of the 507 benchmark tasks 20 times. pass@1 measures average success across all 10,140 attempts. pass@20 measures the share of tasks solved at least once. Observed 20/20 measures the share of tasks that pass every recorded attempt.

Table 1. Qwen3.8-27B results before and after 50 steps of GRPO on the offline-selected training pool.

Training sharply increased repeatable success, with a small decline in at-least-once coverage. The rest of the post explains how we selected practice tasks, built the reward loop, and measured that tradeoff.

What does that improvement look like on one task? A traveler requests a room downgrade, but company policy requires manager approval first. Before training, the agent changed the booking and issued refunds without approval in 15 of 20 attempts. After RL fine-tuning, it preserved the booking and payment state in all 20.

Figure 2. One corporate hotel-booking task, 20 attempts per model. The base Qwen3.8-27B model changed the booking without required manager approval in 15 attempts. The RL fine-tuned model preserved booking and payment state in all 20; all expected records matched in 19.

In a hurry? The headline result is above. The implementation is in Run the training stack .

ThinkingBox-Bench grades agents on the database records they leave behind. Each of its 507 tasks starts a real backend, hands the agent a set of MCP tools and a simulated LLM user with private context, and at the end runs executable checks against the terminal database state. Checks are against the backend record that needs to be correct, not the specific tool calls. This incentivizes the model to discover possibly new solution paths rather than “rediscover” the human-backed solution, that might be suboptimal albeit correct.

AI 투자 불안에 나스닥 2.6% 급락…반도체지수 6.7%↓ [뉴욕증시 브리핑]

미국 뉴욕증권거래소 트레이딩 플로어에서 한 트레이더가 모니터를 살펴보고 있다./사진=연합뉴스

인공지능(AI) 투자에 대한 불안이 다시 커지면서 뉴욕증시가 22일(현지시간) 기술주 중심으로 급락했다. 예멘 후티 반군의 사우디아라비아 공격으로 국제 유가까지 뛰면서 주가 하락에 영향을 줬다.

이날 뉴욕증권거래소(NYSE)에서 다우존스30산업평균지수는 전장보다 11.89포인트(0.02%) 오른 5만2867.98에 거래를 마쳤다. 반면 스탠더드앤드푸어스(S&P)500지수는 93.74포인트(1.21%) 내린 7663.43에, 기술주 중심의 나스닥종합지수는 694.0포인트(2.6%) 급락한 2만6008.86에 각각 마감했다. 특히 나스닥지수는 지난 6월 이후 가장 큰 낙폭을 보였다.

메타 등 주요 기술 기업의 실적 발표를 계기로 대규모 AI 투자 비용을 어떻게 조달하고, 이에 상응하는 수익을 창출할 수 있을지에 대한 우려가 커지면서 투자심리가 급격히 위축됐다.

메타는 시장 예상을 뛰어넘는 3분기 실적을 발표했지만, AI 투자 확대에 필요한 자금을 확보하기 위해 의결권 없는 새로운 종류의 주식을 발행할 계획이라고 밝혔다.

메타는 올해 자본지출 전망치도 종전 1300억~1450억달러에서 1350억~1450억달러로 하단을 상향 조정했다. 향후 지출 약정액은 지난 7월 약 7000억달러에서 8250억달러로 늘어났다.

특히 메타의 3분기 잉여현금흐름은 마이너스 21억2000만달러로, 상장 이후 처음으로 적자를 냈다.

이에 AI 투자 부담이 기업의 자체 현금 창출 능력을 넘어서는 것 아니냐는 우려가 투자자 사이에서 확산했다.

자산관리회사 베어드 프라이빗 웰스 매니지먼트의 마이클 안토넬리 시장 전략가는 "AI를 둘러싼 우려는 더이상 기술 자체에 관한 것이 아니다"라며 "모두가 어떻게 동시에 자금을 조달할 수 있느냐가 문제"라고 말했다.

이날 메타 주가는 약 7% 급락했다. 엔비디아 (-4.4%)와 마이크론(-6.3%) 등이 포함된 필라델피아 반도체지수도 6.7% 하락했다.

지난 20일 첫 분기 흑자를 발표한 스페이스X 는 9.1% 떨어졌고, 테슬라 도 실망스러운 실적에 3.1% 하락했다.

아마존(-4.6%)과 알파벳(-3.2%) 등 대형 기술기업은 물론 데이터센터 관련 기업들에도 매도세가 집중됐다.

반면 기술주에서 이탈한 자금이 상대적으로 AI 투자 열풍과 거리가 먼 업종으로 이동해 일부 경기방어주와 금융주가 강세를 보였다.

미국 국채로도 자금이 몰리면서 국채 금리가 급락했다. 미국 10년 만기 국채 금리는 이날 0.193%포인트 하락한 4.952%로 마감했다. 이는 2023년 3월 미국 지역은행 위기 이후 일간 최대 낙폭이다.

중동 지역의 지정학적 긴장이 고조되면서 국제 유가가 급등한 것도 투자심리를 짓눌렀다. 친이란 성향 예멘 후티 반군이 사우디에 대한 공격을 강화하면서 브렌트유 가격은 배럴당 113달러를 넘어섰다. 이는 지난 5월 이후 가장 높은 수준이다.

items.summary: According to a Circle shareholder, the US president’s “corruption” through USD1 left the company unable to compete with stablecoins, harming USDC.
items.content:
According to a Circle shareholder, the US president’s “corruption” through USD1 left the company unable to compete with stablecoins, harming USDC.

Update (Oct. 22, 10:27 pm UTC): This article has been updated to include a statement from the White House.

A shareholder for Circle Internet Financial, the company behind the USDC (USDC) stablecoin, filed a lawsuit against US President Donald Trump, his family’s crypto company World Liberty Financial, affiliate entities, and US Special Envoy to the Middle East Steve Witkoff over a $2 billion deal between a foreign government entity and Binance.

In a Thursday filing in the US District Court for the District of Columbia, Circle shareholder J. Benjamin Greenberg alleged that Trump, Witkoff and World Liberty caused harm to Circle by creating a pathway for foreign governments to funnel money using the Trump family crypto company’s USD1 stablecoin. This “brazen corruption,” according to Greenberg, leaves Circle “unable to compete” in the stablecoin market with its USDC.

Central to the Circle shareholder’s allegations is an Abu Dhabi entity, MGX, tied to the United Arab Emirates royalty, which invested $2 billion into cryptocurrency exchange Binance using the USD1 stablecoin in 2025. The Wall Street Journal reported in February that another investment vehicle backed by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan agreed to purchase a 49% stake in World Liberty for $500 million.

“By accepting hundreds of millions of dollars from a foreign government, the President and his companies have diverted business from [Circle],” alleged Greenberg, adding:

Related: Trump didn‘t mention ‘crypto’ once in White House cybercrime roundtable

Greenberg reported holding 10,000 ordinary shares of Circle as part of his reasons for the lawsuit. He petitioned the court to declare that Trump violated the US Constitution’s Foreign Emoluments Clause through the crypto deals and to issue injunctions preventing the president and Witkoff from pursuing similar financial interests without Congress’ consent.

Zach Witkoff, the son of the Witkoff named in the lawsuit, is a World Liberty co-founder. Trump and his three sons are also co-founders of the crypto venture.

A Circle spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the company “did not initiate, direct, authorize, or participate in the filing,” declining to comment on pending litigation. White House spokesperson Anna Kelly said that Trump had “no conflicts of interest“ with his crypto investments, calling the lawsuit “frivolous.“ A spokesperson for World Liberty did not respond to a request for comment on the lawsuit.

The US president and his family are tied to several crypto ventures that Trump reported netted him $1.4 billion in 2025, while also costing investors about $4.7 billion, according to reporting by the nonprofit consumer advocacy organization Public Citizen. The crypto ventures are just a few of many controversial deals Trump faces scrutiny over, including accepting a jet from the government of Qatar.

With less than two weeks until the 2026 midterms and early voting having already started in some US states, Democrats running for reelection are using Trump’s crypto deals as a wedge issue for voters to support candidates in their party. Last week, Senator Mark Warner released a campaign ad highlighting that the president made ”more than $600 million alone from the crypto memecoin.”

items.content:
"24조6000억 일감 어쩌라고"…이틀 새 12% 급락에 '비명' [종목+]

LIG디펜스앤에어로스페이스 (LIG D&A·옛 LIG넥스원)가 방위사업청으로부터 국가계약법상 최고 수준인 24개월 입찰 참가 자격 제한 처분을 받았다는 소식에 주가가 연일 급락했다. 다만 증권가에서는 방사청 제재로 국내 수주 불확실성이 커졌으나 이 사안이 단기 실적과 해외 수주에 미치는 영향은 제한적이라는 분석을 내놨다.

23일 한국거래소에 따르면 뇌물 및 원가 부정을 저지른 혐의를 받는 LIG D&A는 방위사업청의 제재 소식이 전해진 후 2거래일 연속 하락했다. LIG D&A는 지난 21일 9.03% 떨어진 데 이어 전날에도 3.11% 내렸다. 특히 지난 21일에는 유가증권시장에서 장중 매수 사이드카(프로그램 매수 호가 효력 일시정지)까지 발동될 정도로 코스피가 급등했다는 점에서 LIG D&A의 약세가 더욱 두드러졌다.

방사청은 지난 20일 방위사업계약심의위원회를 열어 LIG D&A에 국가계약법상 최고 수준인 24개월 입찰 참가 자격 제한 처분을 내리기로 결정했다고 밝혔다. 이는 지난 8월 검찰이 발표한 LIG D&A의 뇌물·원가 부정 사건에 대한 후속 조치다.

증권가에선 방사청 제재로 국내 수주에 대한 불확실성이 커졌지만, 단기 실적과 해외 수주에 미치는 영향은 제한적이라고 봤다.

이한결 키움증권 연구원은 "2028년까지 국내 신규 수주의 불확실성은 확대되나 향후 1~2년간 방사청의 전력화 일정을 고려하면 연관된 신규 사업 규모는 크지 않을 것"이라고 말했다.

핵심 수주인 장사정포요격체계(LAMD), 중거리 지대공 유도무기체계(M-SAM), 장거리 지대공 유도무기체계(L-SAM) 관련 사업은 대부분 수주가 마무리됐으며, 2028년까지 개발 또는 양산 사업이 진행되고 있어 후속 수주 일정은 2028년 이후 이뤄질 가능성이 높다는 이유에서다.

단기적으로는 KF-21 장거리 공대공유도탄 사업, 전자전기 사업 관련 불확실성이 존재한다. 아울러 장거리 공대공유도탄 사업은 현재 우선협상자로 선정됐으나 최종 계약 체결 이전 제재 효력 발생 시 계약 가능 여부와 관련해 법적 불확실성이 있다.

이 연구원은 "올해 상반기 기준 LIG D&A의 수주잔고 약 24조6000억원 중 국내 수주잔고은 10조5000억원으로 기존 계약은 원칙적으로 유지되고 해외 수출 사업도 직접적인 제재 대상이 아니기 때문에 단기 실적에 미치는 영향은 제한적"이라고 선을 그었다. 이어 "중동 방공망 수주 확대 등 기존 투자 포인트가 훼손되지 않았고, 국내 수주 성과에 미칠 영향도 다소 제한적이라고 판단하기 때문에 업종 내 톱픽 의견을 유지한다"고 설명했다.

향후 집행정지 인용 여부도 변수다. LIG D&A는 제재 처분 집행정지 신청과 취소소송 등을 통해 대응할 방침이다. 법원이 집행정지를 인용하면 신규 사업 참여 제한에 따른 불확실성은 상당 부분 완화될 것으로 보인다. 반면 집행정지가 기각되고 제재가 유지되면 국내 신규 수주 차질은 불가피하다.

한편 조만간 발표될 LIG D&A의 올 3분기 실적은 컨센서스(증권사 추정치 평균)를 밑돌 것이라는 전망이 나온다.

items.title: "탈출 기회 안 주나요" 개미 속타는데…증권가 뜻밖의 전망 [분석+]
items.content:
국내 증시가 반도체주 실적 기대와 금리·물가 불안이 맞서면서 하루 간격으로 출렁이고 있다. 앞서 지난 22일 대장주 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스가 급등 하루 만에 다시 하락하면서 코스피도 전날 상승분을 모두 반납했다. 전문가들은 실적 대비 낮아진 주가가 증시 반등의 동력이 될 것으로 전망했지만, 상승세가 이어지려면 반도체 업황과 물가를 둘러싼 불안이 누그러져야 한다고 진단했다.

23일 한국거래소에 따르면 전날 삼성전자는 9000원(4.03%) 내린 21만4500원에 거래를 마쳤다. SK하이닉스는 7만1000원(5.49%) 떨어진 122만3000원에 마감했다. 전 거래일에는 각각 5.67%, 5.81% 급등했지만, 하루 만에 다시 약세로 돌아섰다.

두 종목은 이번주 들어 하루씩 번갈아 오르고 내렸다. 삼성전자는 지난 19일 1.76% 오른 뒤 20일 2.98% 하락했고, 21일 반등했다가 전날 다시 떨어졌다. SK하이닉스도 같은 기간 상승과 하락을 반복했다.

SK하이닉스는 손자회사 솔리다임의 미국 나스닥시장 상장 추진을 둘러싼 중복상장 논란도 부담으로 작용했다. 이억원 금융위원장은 전날 국회 정무위원회 종합감사에서 솔리다임의 미국 상장이 "중복상장 가이드라인 적용 대상"이라며 (SK하이닉스 모회사) SK스퀘어와 SK하이닉스의 주주충실의무 이행을 강조했다.

하루 간격으로 급등락이 반복되면서 개인투자자도 피로감을 드러냈다. 포털사이트 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스 종목토론방에는 "하도 널뛰니 원래 자리가 어딘지 아무도 모를 듯", "탈출 기회 안 주나" 등 주주들이 불안과 불만을 토로하는 글이 쏟아졌다.

반도체 대형주의 등락에 코스피도 출렁였다. 지수는 지난 19일 1.76% 상승한 뒤 20일 3.73% 하락했고, 21일에는 3.29% 반등했다. 전날에는 다시 201.89포인트(3.52%) 떨어진 5533.77로 거래를 마쳤다.

이처럼 반등이 하루를 넘기지 못하는 배경에는 반도체 이익 전망과 거시경제 여건을 둘러싼 불안이 자리하고 있다는 진단이다. 이은택 KB증권 연구원은 "최근 시장을 누른 핵심 요인은 메모리 반도체 우려와 인플레이션(지속적 물가 상승) 우려"라며 "이 가운데 하나가 완화돼야 시장도 반등의 실마리를 찾을 수 있다"고 짚었다.

다만 증권가에서는 이러한 우려를 감안하더라도 최근 주가 하락이 과도하다는 분석이 나온다. 김동원 KB증권 연구원은 "내년 예상 실적 기준 주가수익비율(PER)은 삼성전자 3.3배, SK하이닉스 2.7배에 불과하다"며 "실적과 주가의 이례적 괴리가 역사적 최저 수준으로 확대된 상태"라고 짚었다.

주가를 짓누른 금리와 인공지능(AI) 투자 관련 불안도 점차 잦아들 것이란 전망이다. 김 연구원은 "미국 10년 만기 국채 금리가 연 5%대 중반에서 단기 고점을 형성한 것으로 판단된다"며 "코어위브 등 네오클라우드 업체의 재무건전성 우려가 과도하게 선반영된 만큼 AI 투자 지속성에 대한 불확실성도 점차 완화될 것"이라고 설명했다.

이러한 불안이 완화되면 시장의 관심도 반도체 수요와 실적으로 돌아올 수 있다는 분석이다. 김 연구원은 "AI 반도체 수요는 공급을 2028년까지 웃돌 것으로 예상된다"며 "11~12월에는 실적과 밸류에이션(실적 대비 주가 수준)의 괴리가 축소되는 과정에서 'W자' 반등이 시작될 전망"이라고 내다봤다.

하장권 한화투자증권 연구원도 주가가 거시경제 부담을 상당 부분 반영한 것으로 평가했다. 하 연구원은 "거시경제 여건은 무겁지만, 가격은 이미 그 이상으로 빠진 상황"이라며 "내년 코스피 목표치는 8500, 예상 범위는 6000~9300으로 제시한다"고 말했다.

실적 기대가 주가 회복으로 이어지려면 반도체 기업이 앞으로도 이익을 꾸준히 낼 수 있다는 신뢰가 뒷받침돼야 한다. 이를 확인할 주요 계기로는 연말 장기공급계약(LTA)과 내년 고대역폭메모리(HBM) 가격 협상이 꼽힌다. 하 연구원은 "LTA는 이익 변동성을 줄이는 장치"라며 "올해 4분기부터 내년 1분기까지는 반도체·IT 하드웨어 중심 대응이 유효하다"고 말했다.

반도체 실적에 대한 신뢰 회복과 함께 살펴야 할 변수는 물가다. 실적 대비 주가가 낮더라도 물가와 금리 부담이 지속되면 반등의 힘이 약해질 수 있어서다. 이은택 연구원은 물가 압력이 낮아지고 있음을 보여주는 경제지표와 국제 유가 하락을 이끌 소식에 주목했다.

이 연구원은 "미국 공급관리협회(ISM) 제조업지수의 가격 지표와 고용지표의 임금이 크게 둔화하는 것이 호재"라며 "이란 협상처럼 국제 유가 하락을 유도할 수 있는 뉴스가 필요하다"고 평가했다.

국내에서도 추가 긴축 가능성은 남아있다. 한국은행 금융통화위원회는 전날 기준금리를 연 3.00%로 동결했지만, 통화정책방향문에서 '추가 인상의 시기와 속도 등을 결정'한다는 문구를 유지했다. 지난 7~8월 연속 인상 이후 숨 고르기에 나섰으나 물가에 대한 경계는 이어간 셈이다.

김연지 기자는 한경닷컴 증권부에서 국내 주식시장과 상장사, 증권업계 및 금융투자상품을 취재하고 있습니다. 2023년부터 경제 분야를 취재해 왔으며, 기업 실적과 산업 변화, 시장 수급을 바탕으로 주가가 움직이는 배경을 짚는 기사를 씁니다. 퇴직연금 시장과 연금 투자 흐름을 분석하는 기획 시리즈 "연금 빌드업"도 연재하고 있습니다. 복잡한 금융시장과 투자 정보를 독자의 눈높이에서 풀어내고, 합리적인 투자 판단과 노후 자산 설계에 도움이 되는 인사이트를 전하는 기자가 되고자 합니다.

items.content:
Railway warns devs to rotate secrets after potential breach

Cloud hosting provider Railway published an urgent warning to users after detecting suspicious activity on its systems that store customer environment variables earlier this week.

The company says its investigation indicates that, in some cases, an unauthorized third party may have obtained decrypted variables and urges all users to proactively rotate secrets and credentials.

“Our investigation to date indicates that an unauthorized third party may have accessed encrypted environment variables and, for some of them, obtained the decrypted contents,” Railway says.

“Environment variables may contain secrets such as API keys or database and registry credentials,” the company clarifies.

Railway is a cloud platform for developers to deploy and run applications, APIs, databases, and various backend services. It has around 4.8 million users and hosts more than 16 million services.

The service stores deployment-related configuration settings and credentials in environment variables, which the incident exposed.

Railway says the incident was part of a series of attacks targeting AI inference providers, which were notified directly and advised to revoke all their keys as a precaution.

AI inference providers are services that run AI models and return answers to Railway-hosted applications .

Although initial analysis suggests only a subset of users may be affected, Railway urges all users to immediately rotate environment variables and secrets stored on the platform, including private registry credentials, and check associated service logs for unusual activity.

Railway also said it has paused all deployments until the investigation completes, so users cannot roll out new versions during this time.

According to the latest status page update , as of October 22 at 08:44 UTC, Railway had restored builds for Pro and Enterprise workspaces, but deployments remained delayed, with many queued.

Builds had not yet resumed for Hobby, Free, and Trial workspaces, with restoration planned in that order.

items.title: Toronto crime tips org freezes operations after details of data breach come to light
items.summary: Late Wednesday night the Toronto chapter of Crime Stoppers broke ranks with the national association, revealing a timeline showing what it knew and when along with an announcement that it will pause operations.
items.content:
Image: N A V / Unsplash Toronto crime tips org freezes operations after details of data breach come to light

A Toronto crime prevention program that long promised witnesses a safe space to anonymously report tips froze its operations late Wednesday night, hours after a Canadian news outlet reported that more than 1.5 million tips from Crime Stoppers chapters across the country were exposed in a data breach.

Crime Stoppers urges people not to provide their names when submitting information, but reporters at Canada’s CBC broadcaster were able to reach more than a dozen tipsters by reviewing the hacked data made available to them in March by Distributed Denial of Secrets (DDoSecrets).

About half of the 1.5 million leaked tips CBC studied — some dating back 25 years — contained personal information, the outlet reported.

While Canadian Crime Stoppers Association and individual chapters, including Toronto’s, had confirmed the breach in the days after the hack, they offered no detail about what was exposed, blaming the lack of information on vendor Navigate360 and its subsidiary, P3 Global Intel.

But late Wednesday night the Toronto chapter broke ranks with the national association, revealing a timeline showing what it knew and when along with an announcement that it will pause operations.

“Since 1984, people in Toronto have come to Toronto Crime Stoppers because we promised they could stay anonymous,” Sean Sportun, chair of Toronto Crime Stoppers, said in a statement . “This week’s reporting shows that for some of them, that promise was broken. We are deeply sorry.”

The Toronto organization said it has directed Navigate360 to immediately stop taking tips and no longer process any new information. It also has told Canada’s National Anonymous Call Centre to stop receiving and processing tips meant for Toronto Crime Stoppers, according to the statement.

“Until we have a safer way to protect you, please do not send us tips by phone, online, or through the app,” the statement said.

The organization is looking for a way to take tips on a truly anonymous basis, it said.

“For more than 40 years, people in Toronto have relied on Crime Stoppers to share what they know without giving their name: a witness afraid of retaliation, a neighbour who can’t be seen talking to police, someone reporting a person close to them,” the statement said.

“Their courage has helped solve crimes, prevent tragedies, and save lives. Pausing our program means that option isn’t available now, and we did not make this decision lightly. We are pausing because those people deserve a system we can fully stand behind.”

Canadian Crime Stoppers Association and Navigate360 did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Navigate360 told Toronto Crime Stoppers that the stolen data contained 176,859 Toronto tips, which were reported between January 2022 and November 2025, the Toronto chapter’s statement said. The vendor also told Toronto Crime Stoppers that it had found 14,973 names in those tips, but could not say if the names belonged to tipsters, suspects or both.

Toronto Crime Stoppers has made “numerous requests” through their lawyers for the text of the stolen tips, but Navigate360 has not responded, the statement said.

“Since March, Navigate360 has told us repeatedly that P3 is secure,” the statement said. “In April, it told us Toronto’s data had not been taken. When it told us in June that Toronto’s data was affected, it didn’t say what was exposed.”

A hacktivist collective known as Internet Yiff Machine took responsibility for the March breach, saying its goal was to prove that Navigate360 and P3 Global Intel lied about their capabilities.

The new service aims to bring onchain trading data into institutional financial systems as tokenized stock markets expand and face growing scrutiny.

Blockchain analytics platform Dune has launched real-time market data feeds covering more than 200 onchain trading venues, aiming to bring decentralized market activity into the trading systems used by traditional financial institutions.

The new service provides trade data from 12 blockchains, including Ethereum, Solana, Base and XLayer, roughly one second after execution, according to a Thursday announcement.

The feeds cover spot trading across decentralized exchanges, as well as perpetual futures trading on Hyperliquid and Lighter, with standardized data on prices, trade sizes and transaction details across markets.

According to Dune co-founder and CEO Fredrik Haga, quant funds, market makers, asset managers and bank trading desks are among the first clients using the service, although he declined to identify them, citing nondisclosure agreements. Dune said the firms use the data to assess liquidity, compare prices across venues and evaluate trading strategies before committing capital.

“Most institutions are watching onchain markets first, because they can’t price these assets properly without them anymore,” Haga said. He expects direct onchain trading to follow as liquidity improves and regulatory rules catch up, adding:

Related: Ondo lets institutions convert stocks directly into tokenized shares

The market for tokenized stocks has grown sharply over the past year, but fragmented liquidity and disputes over whether companies should have a say in how their shares are traded onchain have raised questions about the market’s development.

Recently, tensions surfaced around OKXICE, a joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange. The venture announced plans for a tokenized stock trading platform on Oct. 4, but has since faced objections from several publicly traded companies.

So far, 16 companies, including Microsoft, Alphabet and Goldman Sachs, have filed objections to having their shares traded on the proposed platform, although they did not specify their reasons.

Beyond issuer objections, market fragmentation poses another concern. In May, Tiger Research director Ryan Yoon warned that trading the same tokenized stocks across multiple blockchain platforms could create price discrepancies , increase slippage and reduce market efficiency.

According to RWA.xyz data , the distributed value of tokenized stocks has reached $3.58 billion, up from about $627 million a year earlier, a roughly 470% increase.

items.summary: Japanese gaming giant Capcom has confirmed that hackers breached its membership service, CAPCOM ID, exposing more than 11.7 million customer email addresses and associated information. [...]
items.content:
Capcom confirms data breach affecting 11.7 million accounts

Japanese gaming giant Capcom has confirmed that hackers breached its membership service, CAPCOM ID, exposing more than 11.7 million customer email addresses and associated information.

Apart from emails, exposed data includes account creation date, last login timestamp, number of logins, and the IP address used at the last login.

Capcom found that for a small subset of 43 accounts, dates of birth, gender, nicknames, and countries were also exposed.

For another subset of 196 accounts, the hackers changed the CAPCOM ID login passwords in an attempt to lock the owners out, but the company took action and reset them.

In an alert today , the gaming company says that passwords for all other registered members have not been exposed and that credit card information remained unaffected.

Capcom is a Japanese video game developer and publisher known for franchises such as Resident Evil, Monster Hunter, Street Fighter, and Mega Man. The company has 4,000 employees and an annual revenue of $1.24 billion.

CAPCOM ID is the company’s shared account system used for accessing its web services and playing some of its online games.

Although the timing of the breach remains unclear, Capcom said it detected suspicious activity and confirmed unauthorized access on October 19.

An investigation was launched immediately, and by the following day, it was clear that customer information had been compromised.

October 21, the company reported the  incident to the police and to Japan’s Personal Information Protection Commission.

Capcom said its online services remain unaffected, but cautioned users to stay vigilant for unsolicited communications and emails requesting additional information, or messages containing URLs and attachments.

During the investigation, Capcom identified the intrusion method and implemented security measures to prevent similar incidents. However, no details related to the initial access have been shared.

The gaming firm also says it will notify affected customers in stages, likely due to the large volume of affected accounts, but it has established region-specific communication channels to submit support requests.

In November 2020, Capcom suffered an attack claimed by the Ragnar Locker ransomware gang , in which attackers claimed to have stolen 1 TB of data . The company subsequently warned that up to 390,000 people could be affected.

In April 2021, Capcom disclosed that the attackers had gained access through an old VPN device .

items.title: Winklevoss PAC moves into Texas Senate race with $81K ad buy
items.summary: While crypto-aligned PACs have stepped up spending in Ohio, a committee launched by the co-founders of crypto exchange Gemini made one of its first forays into the Lone Star State.
items.content:
While crypto-aligned PACs have stepped up spending in Ohio, a committee launched by the co-founders of crypto exchange Gemini made one of its first forays into the Lone Star State.

Digital Freedom Fund, the Super political action committee (PAC) launched by Gemini co-founders Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss in 2025, announced additional expenditures for US Senate races in the 2026 midterm elections, attempting to influence voters in Texas, Iowa and Ohio.

In a Tuesday filing with the US Federal Election Commission (FEC), the Digital Freedom Fund reported its first spending on ads to support Republican candidate Ken Paxton for one of Texas’ Senate seats. According to the PAC, it had spent more than $81,000 on direct mail media to support Paxton and oppose Democratic candidate James Talarico, with early voting having already begun in the state.

The Winklevoss-backed Super PAC, which reported raising about $34 million as of Sept. 30, did not limit its spending to Texas, reporting involvement in other key midterm election races using ads. Digital Freedom Fund disclosed additional expenditures in Ohio’s Senate race between Republican Jon Husted and Democrat Sherrod Brown, bringing the PAC’s total support for Husted to about $7 million.

The expenditures into candidates that could support crypto policies and laws come as event contracts on prediction market platforms Kalshi and Polymarket heavily favored Democrats retaking majority control of the House of Representatives and Senate in 2027. Whichever party holds a majority in each chamber would have a significant impact on passing legislation like the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, a market structure bill that failed to pass a procedural vote in the Senate last month.

Related: PACs laud Texas primary wins, look to back more pro-crypto candidates

Paxton already benefitted from $500,000 in supportive ads ahead of the May Republican primary, in which he defeated incumbent Senator John Cornyn. The ads, funded by the Anchorage Digital- and Cantor Fitzgerald-backed Fellowship PAC, went through the Nxum Group, a marketing company co-founded by Bo Hines, a former crypto adviser to US President Donald Trump who became CEO of Tether US after leaving the White House.

According to an October Wall Street Journal report, Nxum profited from Hines’ role in government, as he helped push a stablecoin bill while keeping a stake in the company. Nxum reportedly received $6.3 million as part of a deal with stablecoin issuer Tether, the first payment of which went through while Hines was still at the White House.

Early voting began in Texas on Oct. 19, with Election Day coming up on Nov. 3. Cointelegraph reached out to the Talarico and Paxton campaign teams for comment but did not receive an immediate response.

Fairshake, a separate PAC aligned with the interests of the crypto industry and largely funded by Ripple Labs, Coinbase and Andreessen Horowitz, reported more than $13 million combined in spending on a direct mail campaign to support what it considered to be “pro-crypto” candidates this week. The PAC’s latest FEC filing showed more than $4 million to oppose Independent candidate Dan Osborn in Nebraska’s Senate race and an additional $9 million to support Husted over Brown.

While the battle for Ohio’s Senate between Brown and Husted has seen significant spending by PACs — Fairshake had invested about $56 million as of Wednesday and Digital Freedom Fund reported $7 million in total media purchases — Texas races have also spawned interest from Republican donors looking to prevent the state potentially losing Senate and gubernatorial seats to Democrats for the first time in more than 30 years.

FEC filings showed that Elon Musk, the world’s richest person and founder of SpaceX, had poured more than $150 million into the Senate Leadership Fund. The PAC, supporting Republican Senate candidates, sent the same amount Musk donated to the Texas PAC, which has supported Paxton through ads.

items.title: LiteLLM release pipeline hacked to distribute info-stealer malware
items.summary: Hackers compromised the LiteLLM project's PyPI package and published malicious Docker images with a payload that steals credentials, secrets, and environment variables. [...]
items.content:
LiteLLM release pipeline hacked to distribute info-stealer malware

Hackers compromised the LiteLLM project’s PyPI package and published malicious Docker images with a payload that steals credentials, secrets, and environment variables.

The supply-chain attack affected all PyPI wheels (.whl installation packages) for LiteLLM version 1.107.0, impacting Windows, Linux, and macOS systems.

LiteLLM is an open-source Python SDK and AI gateway that enables applications to access AI models from different providers through a common API.

It is a massively popular project with 61,800 GitHub stars, 92 million monthly downloads on PyPI, and is used by high-profile companies like NVIDIA, Netflix, AT&T, and Okta.

The project says that the release pipeline was compromised on October 21 and a threat actor pushed version 1.107.0 to the Docker registry and PyPI.

"This version contained compiled malware which steals credentials and loads remote-code execution tools," the maintainer says, adding that customers running the private enterprise were not impacted.

In a post-mortem of the incident, the maintainer says that the following LiteLLM artifacts were affected in the attack:

PyPI: litellm==1.107.0: all seven wheels, live from 11:39:51 to 13:23 UTC

Docker Hub: v1.107.0, latest, main-latest, and main-stable: pointed to compromised image index sha256:1bbcb1443bc962e45f5aad53fe3d2c30600e0379715fb6c664cdd3ac126c339e from 11:46:56 to 14:20 UTC

GHCR: v1.107.0, latest, main-latest, and main-stable: pointed to the compromised image indexes below from 11:46:56 UTC until they were made unavailable by 13:51 UTC

ghcr.io/berriai/litellm: sha256:1bbcb1443bc9…

ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database: sha256:c00f9d92c427…

ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-non_root: sha256:7b00e91cd2fe…

Multiple application security companies detected the attack within six minutes of publishing the malicious LiteLLM version and analyzed the payload.

According to the researchers, the attacker did not touch the LiteLLM application code and modified only the installation package to place three malicious files (cook.pth, cook.py, and sitecustomize.py) in the environment's Python’s library directory.

"During normal startup, Python processes executable .pth lines and then attempts to import sitecustomize," Socket researchers explain .

Endor Labs notes that this way the payloads are executed before the application every time Python is launched in the environment. Running Python or pip to investigate an affected installation also triggered the malware.

The malware targeted the following data:

Cloud and deployment credentials: AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Kubernetes, Docker, and infrastructure-management secrets.

AI credentials and configuration: Authentication files for AI development tools, plus LiteLLM’s stored provider credentials and model settings.

Developer secrets and private keys: Git, GitHub, npm, PyPI, and CI/CD credentials; .env files; SSH, GPG, and TLS keys.

Browser data: Saved login, cookie, autofill/payment, and browsing-history databases.

Host and runtime data: Environment variables, shell and application histories, and system and network information.

The stolen data is encrypted using an AES-256-CBC key that is encrypted with an RSA-4096 key and then uploaded to ‘litellm[.]dev/healthcheck’

One of the malicious files, sitecustomize.py, launches a detached loader that checks a GitHub-hosted pointer every hour and downloads Python from an external server for execution on the host.

The malicious packages have been removed, but potentially impacted users should stop affected deployments and inspect environments without launching the Python interpreter.

Infected systems should be isolated and rebuilt from clean backups, and all exposed secrets should be rotated immediately.

Removing the LiteLLM package directory alone may leave startup files or an active loader behind.

Currently, the recommended recovery version is LiteLLM 1.106.2, which is the latest clean release…

Concerns have swirled over the access that consumers are increasingly entrusting to AI agents. Now, security services are trying to catch up.

Password manager 1Password on Thursday launched a new tool by which users can allow agents to log into their personal accounts on their behalf, without the agent ever having access to a user’s credentials.

The new platform, dubbed 1Password for Agents , accomplishes this by creating a system of communication between the agent, the user, and the password manager. When an agent attempts to log in on a user’s behalf, a unique digital key is sent to 1Password to confirm the agent’s digital identity. The user is then sent an alert about the login attempt and can personally confirm the request. 1Password then signs in the agent, filling in the credentials on the digital assistant’s behalf, which allows it to log in and complete whatever task is at hand.

1Password for Agents allows users to choose their agent of choice — whether that’s Claude Duet from Anthropic, OpenAI’s Dots or ChatGPT Work, Grok Bot, Meta’s Muse, or agents from Town, which is an AI assistant startup. The company says it is working with other companies to expand the service.

“Handing over a password, secret, or credential is a common shortcut to an agent, but can leave people with sensitive information in places they can no longer control as a copy gets saved for the next time,” the company said in a blog post . “1Password for Agents gives people a trusted way to delegate tasks to personal AI agents while keeping control of the passwords, secrets, and credentials those tasks require.”

Online agentic activity has increasingly unsettled major institutions. Indeed, 1Password’s new platform is launching on the same day that Axios reports that U.S. banks have begun to detect agentic activity inside user accounts.

This isn’t necessarily a case of rogue agents pilfering accounts but, rather, an example of how consumers are increasingly allowing automated services to act on their behalf, including on financial matters. However, the potential for agent-related problems is still large. The big issue appears to be that most banks cannot tell if the agentic activity is tied to user requests or not.

Bankers interviewed by the outlet described the situation as “horrifying,” and a Chase spokesperson interviewed by Axios additionally told the outlet that customers “should not give their usernames and passwords to anyone.”

items.content:
Attackers are exploiting a zero-day SQL injection flaw in Arista's VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO), the central management system for VeloCloud SD-WAN networks, the company said in an advisory on October 22.

The flaw lets anyone who can log in to the orchestrator, even with a read-only customer account, gain operator privileges, the top level of control over it.

For on-premises orchestrators, the fix is in VCO 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10, and 6.4.2.12, while Hosted and Dedicated orchestrators have already been patched.

The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-114625 and rated 9.9 on the CVSS scale. Orchestrators running the releases that fixed the VCO flaws exploited in July and September are still affected, because those releases are older than the new fixes.

Arista bought the VeloCloud SD-WAN product line from Broadcom, announcing the deal in July 2025. The products were earlier known as VMware SD-WAN by VeloCloud.

To exploit the flaw, an attacker needs network access to the orchestrator's web interface and a valid login. The minimum role is Enterprise Read Only, the lowest built-in role for customer users. VCO is exposed by default, and no VCO setting prevents the exposure.

In VCO, operators create the customer and partner accounts, and each partner can manage a group of customers. The flaw allows an attacker to act as a local superuser, a role with full access . It may also allow an attacker to affect the VCO host itself and expose, modify, or disrupt the orchestrator and the data it manages.

The advisory does not say when the attacks began, which orchestrators were hit, or what the attackers did after exploiting the flaw.

The new flaw is the third in VCO since late July that Arista has reported as exploited, and the first of the three that requires a login. Neither the July flaw (CVE-2026-16812) nor the September flaw (CVE-2026-93952) needed one.

Each affected release train has its own fix, shown here beside the release that fixed September's flaw on the same train.

VeloCloud Gateway and VeloCloud Edge are not affected. The 7.0 release train is not on the list, and Arista says any release not on the list is not vulnerable.

Arista has not checked releases that have reached end of support. Customers on an unsupported release train can contact Arista's Technical Assistance Center (TAC) about upgrade options.

As of October 22, September's flaw is fixed only in the 5.2 and 6.4 trains . On 6.1, it affects releases up to 6.1.3.7, and no fixed release is listed. Neither advisory says whether 6.1.3.10 also fixes the September flaw.

Until the fixed release is installed, Arista recommends these steps:

Two IP addresses have been seen carrying out the attacks, according to Arista. Block them and check logs for any sign of them:

Also check VCO web access logs for requests with unusual URL-like path components, encoded characters, references to local or internal services, or high request rates.

If you suspect a compromise, save evidence before fixing anything, where possible. That means the VCO web access, backend application, system and database logs, along with the relevant file-system timestamps.

Regarding the July and September flaws, Arista warned that a compromised orchestrator could also grant attackers access to VeloCloud Edge devices. For this flaw, the advisory does not say whether the risk applies or whether upgrading removes access that an attacker has already gained.

OpenAI made its Decisions API model widely available to users for the first time, entering the market for fast, cheap intelligence that recently made TypeSafe, a startup founded by a former researcher at the frontier lab, a $7.6 billion company .

TypeSafe’s Jev model created a category for deep learning models that act as super classifiers: Given a set of options, they can quickly make choices and offer a confidence rating in their decision. Software developers quickly found that these decision or System One models could replace LLMs in a variety of workflows, operating more quickly and a at dramatically lower cost.

Nikunj Handa, the product lead for OpenAI’s APIs, told TechCrunch that his colleagues saw Jev and said “wow, we we have like a million use cases for this.” Handa’s team sprinted to offer their own version: Rather than building a specifically calibrated decision model, the team took ChatGPT Luna and reconfigured it to speed up the inference and lower the cost.

“The big unlock with Decisions API has been the speed, shrinking things from one to three seconds to 100, 120, 180 milliseconds,” Handa said. “In the future, we may sort of like have specific training to make our models like even better in these ways. But right now, it’s just plain old Luna that gets the job done.”

Announced at the company’s developer day on September 29, the Decisions API became available to all customers on Thursday. OpenAI added new voice and visual modalities to the public version, and worked to ensure lower latency in regions around the world by targeting its inference resources geographically.

In initial trials with customers like Box, Datadog, Ramp, and Speak, engineers used the API to replace OpenAI’s LLMs with higher throughput. Andrew Hsu, the CTO at Speak, which builds AI language tutors, said the Decisions API allowed the company to cut the time between actions from 1.4 seconds to .13 seconds. OpenAI also used the product to improve their Dots voice assistant’s responsiveness.

Still, it’s not clear exactly what makes a good decision model, other than “it works for you” — optimization across intelligence, cost, calibration, and speed seems to differ by workload. TypeSafe CEO Diogo Almeida distrusts benchmarks and urges people to trial the models in their own work, but even TypeSafe released its own rankings last week alongside the release of its latest Jev model, which includes new features including support for images and smart-if statements.

Public benchmarks like the AIM System One Index and the Artificial Analysis Decision Index tend to favor D1 Ultra, a new decision model that Liquid released last week, and Base Lab’s Elephant-1. The latest Jev model remains competitive on both indices, in seventh and third, with OpenAI’s Decision Model falling eighth and fourteenth, respectively. However, TypeSafe’s offerings are, for now, the most widely-queried on OpenRouter.

The most fun Jev benchmark, however, is JevMan , a benchmark where decision models play PacMan; the latest Jev model tops that ranking. Felix Wunderlich, the chief growth officer at Opper AI, which built the benchmark, said the classic game “is an interesting test because of its nonstop stream of quick, high-stakes decisions. At every junction the model must decide where to go in a few hundred milliseconds.”

Where OpenAI’s arguably more capable model may have an advantage is in multi-modality—for image classification, “Luna is extremely powerful and has been showing better calibrations,” Handa told TechCrunch, adding that OpenAI customers want the Decisions API to be more flexible about using images as outputs as well.

items.title: Canva releases its first image generation model
items.summary: Canva is making its new image model available to all users, promising better, more customizable performance at lower costs.
items.content:

Design platform Canva released its first image generation model, called Canva Craft, developed by its research team to compete with same-category models from Google, OpenAI, ByteDance, and Meta.

The company said its model works in two stages. In the first stage, it interprets users’ prompts and creates a plan with details like spatial relationships of elements, relative scale, visual hierarchy, and information for text generation. In the second stage, its model generates an image of up to 2K resolution in a possible 30 different aspect ratios for various platforms.

Canva said that this approach allows it to create images with accurate details of objects and legible text. Plus, users would be able to make precise edits without changing other parts of the image.

The company noted that rather than using photographs, it used designs to train this model using human-designed templates from Canva’s library, including posters, social posts, presentations, infographics, menus, and typography-rich layouts.

That means images generated with Canva Craft could be converted into layered designs using Canva Magic, the company’s image-to-design transformer. Last year, the platform released its own model that understands designs and layers .

Canva Craft is available on the company’s platform to all users, who can access the model from the Dream Lab tab. The model will also be available through the Canva API. Plus, the company plans to support image generation in third-party chatbots like ChatGPT and Gemini through Canva’s MCP.

Canva has used a bunch of image models for generation in its platform, so it’s likely that the new models will help save API costs for the company. It said that besides costs, the new model also allows the platform to have better quality and speed control.

In 2024, Canva acquired media generation platform Leonardo.ai . It said that the researchers from Leonardo contributed to the new image model.

Canva said that it is developing two cost-efficient versions of the model, called Craftfast and Craft-ultrafast, which will be released soon.

The company was on track for $4 billion in revenue last year . However, it cut its growth forecast for 2026 , causing its valuation to reportedly plummet from $42 billion to $35 billion , according to external analysts.

items.title: Indian tech company eMudhra announces withdrawal from certificate business after security incident
items.summary: The issue was publicized by cybersecurity researcher Scott Helme, who published a blog saying that instead of a random 384-bit number, one of the company's private keys was just the number four.
items.content:
Image: Getty via Unsplash+ Indian tech company eMudhra announces withdrawal from certificate business after security incident

One of the only Indian root certificate authorities trusted by major web browsers said it is withdrawing from the global certificate business after facing significant backlash over a security incident this week.

The company, eMudhra, said it was voluntarily withdrawing from the global SSL/TLS certificate business after the private keys of eight of its intermediate certificates were found to be weak, prompting browsers like Firefox , Apple and Chrome to block the certificates.

According to Google, Mozilla and several other companies, the keys could allow attackers to issue fraudulent HTTPS certificates for websites they do not control. An attacker who could intercept a user’s connection could use those certificates to impersonate websites and potentially read or modify traffic.

Cloudflare explained that the certificates were widely trusted by their own system as well as browsers and operating systems. Because of the weak keys, any attacker could create a forged certificate for any domain and use it to impersonate servers to intercept or modify traffic.

The issue was publicized by cybersecurity researcher Scott Helme, who published a blog saying that instead of a random 384-bit number, one of the private keys was just the number four. Others were simply 56 and 115.

eMudhra said this week that the certificates were created during a ceremony in April 2025 and the ”problem was a flaw in one step of the ceremony procedure.” The issue went undetected for 18 months and survived two independent audits before a researcher reverse engineered the weak keys, the company said.

eMudhra’s chairman, V. Srinivasan, said on Thursday that the company revoked the affected certificates within 14 hours of their discovery and claimed there were no compromises or data breaches as a result of the issue.

India’s Ministry of Electronics and IT said it is investigating the incident but defended the company, arguing that “some social media accounts are indulging in fear mongering about the impact of this incident.”

CERT-IN warned in its own alert that an attacker able to exploit the compromised private keys could "potentially impersonate legitimate websites or intercept or modify data exchanged between users and servers, potentially facilitating credential theft, sensitive data exposure and financial fraud."

They added that the ability to issue fraudulent certificates would also enable malicious software to appear to be digitally signed by a trusted publisher.

In the announcement of its withdrawal from the certificate business, Srinivasan said it only accounted for 1% of the company’s revenue but became increasingly costly due to compliance requirements and “complexity.”

Srinivasan blamed “social media amplification” for the increased scrutiny around the company. eMudhra said it will work with browser programs and customers to transition them to other options.

“Revocation and certificate status services will keep running until every issued certificate has expired or been replaced. eMudhra will complete its remaining commitments to the browser root programs, including a full root-cause report,” the company said.

Google noted that eMudhra has committed to working with impacted subscribers to migrate customers off of the impacted root but said it is “closely investigating the ongoing inclusion of eMudhra's remaining CA certificates in the Chrome Root Store.”

Brian Fox, co-founder of cybersecurity firm Sonatype, told Recorded Future News that the issue goes far beyond browsers because certificate trust stores are embedded in dozens of products.

Each may require its own update, rebuild or release, and most organizations don’t have an inventory of where they live, he said.

items.title: Microsoft’s Mustafa Suleyman says its AI outperforms doctors on hard cases as he chases ‘medical superintelligence’
items.summary: Microsoft’s new AI diagnostic system beat generalist doctors on hard cases, according to a study in Science. But most of the improvement seems to come from the AI models underneath, not from Microsoft’s system itself.
items.content:
Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now.

Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW.

Microsoft’s AI diagnostic system correctly diagnosed complex medical cases in a simulation more than twice as often as generalist physicians, according to a study published Thursday in Science. Mustafa Suleyman, Microsoft AI’s CEO, called the result a step toward “medical superintelligence.”

The system, dubbed MAI-DxO (DxO for short), coordinates several AI agents that act like a panel of doctors. They question a patient, order tests, and debate a diagnosis.

In a simulation using complex cases from the New England Journal of Medicine, it was correct 83% of the time. Primary care doctors and general internists, working individually with reference materials, were correct 36% of the time. One note: Cases this complex are usually handled by specialists or physician teams, who weren’t part of the comparison.

“There is something very substantial and exciting here,” Dominic King, vice president of Health at Microsoft AI, told TechCrunch. “The biggest challenge in healthcare delivery at the moment is the growing mismatch between demand and supply of medical expertise.”

In publishing these results , Microsoft joins Go o gle and OpenAI in claiming that its AI can match or outperform doctors.

The study’s own data suggests that much of the improvement comes from more powerful underlying AI models, with Microsoft’s orchestration system adding gains on top.

Microsoft tested MAI-DxO with models from several companies, including OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Meta, and DeepSeek, but its best results came with OpenAI’s GPT-5 and GPT-5.5.

Microsoft measured DxO on cost as well as accuracy, meaning the estimated cost of running the AI on each case. On its own with a short, basic prompt, GPT-5 scored 78.9% on complex cases at about $8,400 per case. DxO cut that cost by about $3,000 but raised accuracy by only about four points. On emergency department cases, there was little improvement in either accuracy or cost improvement between GPT-5 on its own and with the assist from DxO.

With GPT-5.5, a newer model released in April 2026, the results split. On complex cases, DxO increased GPT-5.5’s accuracy score from 72% to nearly 87% at a slightly cheaper cost. However, the gains once again didn’t show up on emergency department cases. Both (with and without DxO) scored about 85% at a similar cost.

DxO helps most on complex cases and with less capable AI models. Gemini 2.5 Flash, for example, scored 46.4% on its own but nearly 69% with DxO. Even so, the gap between the weaker and stronger models was larger than the boost DxO provided.

Microsoft’s researchers said that accuracy gains naturally shrink as models approach the theoretical maximum. “The DxO orchestration helps with the broader challenge of optimization both accuracy and cost,” a spokesperson added.

Suleyman, who leads Microsoft’s effort to build its own frontier AI, told TechCrunch that the company is working with the Mayo Clinic to train a foundation model for healthcare, with release planned for next year. He believes this model will enable the company to “make really enormous leaps here,” and says DxO is part of the foundational infrastructure Microsoft is building to see real breakthroughs in healthcare.

“I really believe that in 2027, we will be on the verge of a coding style breakthrough for medical records,” Suleyman said. “I think we’re going to be able to stream highly accurate predictions about how a medical record might unfold, and obviously that kind of foresight for a clinician is gold dust.”

Suleyman has spent his career trying to use AI to solve medical issues. He was previously a co-founder of DeepMind, which was acquired by Google in 2014. 국립항공박물관 회원 1만1,029명의 개인정보가 유출되고, 박물관 교육 안내에 사용되는 전화번호를 통해 스미싱 문자까지 발송된 문제가 국정감사에서 제기됐다. 공공기관의 개인정보 유출이 이용자를 대상으로 한 사기성 문자 발송 문제와 함께 드러났다는 점에서 보안관리 체계와 사고 이후 대응의 적절성이 쟁점으로 떠올랐다.

22일 국정감사 관련 공개 내용에 따르면 국립항공박물관에서 회원 1만1,029명의 개인정보가 유출된 사실과 함께 박물관 교육 안내번호를 이용한 스미싱 문자 발송 문제가 확인됐다.

스미싱은 공공기관이나 기업 등을 사칭한 문자메시지로 이용자를 속여 악성 인터넷주소에 접속하도록 유도하거나 개인정보와 금융정보를 탈취하는 사이버 범죄 수법이다.

특히 이번 사안은 박물관의 교육 안내에 사용되는 번호가 악용됐다는 점에서 주목된다. 이용자들이 평소 안내를 받던 번호로 사기성 문자를 수신할 경우 정상적인 기관 안내로 오인할 가능성이 있기 때문이다.

다만 개인정보 유출과 스미싱 문자 발송 사이의 구체적인 기술적 연관성은 추가 확인이 필요하다.

사고 이후 피해자 보호 조치도 중요한 쟁점이다. 개인정보 유출 사실을 회원들에게 신속하게 알렸는지, 의심 문자에 대한 주의 안내가 충분했는지, 문자에 포함된 인터넷주소를 통한 추가 피해가 발생했는지 등을 확인할 필요가 있다.

items.title: A16z is the latest VC giant to widen bets beyond crypto and into AI and emerging tech
items.content:
Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), one of crypto's most influential venture capital backers, is dropping "crypto" from the name of its investment arm and expanding into artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies, becoming the latest major crypto investor to broaden its focus.

The Silicon Valley firm is renaming its a16z Crypto fund to a16z Frontier, targeting startups developing technologies and markets that may take years to mature, general partner Chris Dixon said in a Thursday blog post .

The move doesn't mean a16z is abandoning digital assets. The firm will continue backing crypto companies and advocating for crypto regulation, Dixon said.

"This is an expansion: we will continue to invest in crypto and related ventures and advocate for sensible crypto regulation," he wrote.

The VC giant had played a significant role in shaping the crypto industry. An early Coinbase investor, the firm also backed major blockchain projects including Solana (SOL) and decentralized exchange Uniswap (UNI), while pouring billions into crypto startups and becoming a prominent voice in U.S. policy debates.

The company’s decision is the latest example of a broader pivot among venture capital firms that made their names in crypto but are now looking beyond digital assets.

Paradigm raised $1.2 billion in July to invest in AI, robotics and other technologies, while Framework Ventures raised $400 million in June to expand into AI, energy, fintech and tokenization. Haun Ventures also broadened its focus toward AI and financial services with a $1 billion fundraising in May.

A16z Frontier will explore AI-powered products, autonomous machines and networks connecting people and AI agents. Dixon sees blockchains playing a role in those networks by enabling payments and transactions between machines.

Dixon argued that as blockchain technology spreads into mainstream finance, the distinction between crypto companies and other businesses is becoming less useful.

"Wall Street and fintech companies now regularly launch products built on blockchains,” he wrote. “Does that make them crypto companies? The label matters less now."

Dixon said he will lead the fund alongside a16z founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz and general partners Eddy Lazzarin and Guy Wuollet.

items.content:
최근 금융권에서 해킹과 개인정보 유출 사고가 잇따르고 있지만, 국내 금융회사의 정보보호 전담인력은 전체 정보기술(IT) 인력의 10%에도 미치지 못하는 것으로 나타났다. 정보보호 업무를 총괄하는 최고책임자(CISO)도 4명 중 1명 이상이 다른 업무를 겸직하고 있어 금융권의 보안 대응 역량을 강화해야 한다는 지적이 제기됐다.

22일 국회 재정경제기획위원회 소속 강민국 국민의힘 의원이 금융감독원으로부터 제출받은 '국내 금융업권 IT 및 정보보호 인력·예산 현황'에 따르면, 올해 6월 말 기준 은행·저축은행·증권·자산운용·생명보험·손해보험·카드 등 7개 금융업권의 전체 임직원은 22만5,145명으로 집계됐다.

이 가운데 IT 인력은 2만7,508명(전체 임직원의 12.2%)이며, 정보보호 인력은 2,654명으로 IT 인력의 9.6%에 불과했다.

금융권 정보보호 인력 비중은 2023년과 2024년 각각 9.0%, 2025년 9.1%로 수년째 10%를 밑돌고 있다.

업권별 정보보호 인력 비중은 자산운용사가 15.5%로 가장 높았으며, 저축은행 14.0%, 카드사 12.7%, 손해보험사 10.0% 순이었다. 반면 증권사는 9.5%, 은행은 8.8%, 생명보험사는 8.4%로 전체 평균에도 미치지 못했다.

특히 자산운용업권은 지난해 말 20.4%에서 올해 6월 말 15.5%로 4.9%포인트 감소했다. 개별 금융회사 중에서도 우리은행의 정보보호 인력이 101명에서 92명으로, 비씨카드는 34명에서 17명으로 줄어든 것으로 나타났다.

정보보호 예산도 업권별 차이가 컸다. 올해 6월 말 기준 7개 금융업권의 전체 IT 예산은 14조2,396억원이며, 이 가운데 정보보호 예산은 1조6,726억원으로 11.7%를 차지했다.

업권별 정보보호 예산 비중은 자산운용사가 19.3%, 저축은행 17.2%, 카드사 14.2%로 상대적으로 높았다. 반면 은행은 11.3%, 생명보험 11.1%, 증권 10.9%로 전체 평균보다 낮았다. 은행과 자산운용업권의 정보보호 예산 비중은 전년보다 각각 0.4%포인트, 0.3%포인트 감소했다.

정보보호 책임자의 겸직 문제도 확인됐다. 조사 대상 금융업권에서 지정된 CISO는 총 92명으로, 이 가운데 전임자는 68명(73.9%)이었다. 나머지 24명(26.1%)은 다른 업무를 함께 수행하고 있었다.

특히 저축은행은 CISO 9명 중 전임자가 4명에 그쳤으며, 증권업권도 29명 중 18명만 전임으로 조사됐다. 다만 겸직 자체가 곧 법규 위반이나 보안관리 부실을 의미하는 것은 아니며, 금융회사별 법적 의무와 실제 업무 수행체계를 함께 살펴볼 필요가 있다.

이번 조사 결과는 금융권의 정보보호 인력과 예산이 소폭 증가하고 있음에도 사이버 위협에 대응할 충분한 전문인력과 독립적인 보안관리 체계를 확보하고 있는지 점검할 필요가 있음을 보여준다. 특히 보안인력 비율뿐 아니라 실제 취약점 점검과 침해사고 대응에 투입할 수 있는 인력, CISO의 예산·인사 권한 등이 중요하다는 분석이다.

강민국 의원은 “최근 수년간 업권을 가리지 않고 사이버 위협이 증가하는 상황에서도 금융업권의 정보보호 인력 비중이 10%에도 미치지 못하는 것은 금융소비자의 개인정보 보호를 소홀히 하는 것”이라며 “금융당국은 사이버 보안 위협에 대응할 수 있도록 정보보호 인력과 예산 기준을 전자금융거래법 하위 규정에 명문화하고, 금융회사도 AI 보안 전문가와 화이트해커 등 전문인력 채용을 확대해야 한다”고 강조했다.

items.title: Major US banks are locking out AI agents that log in with customer credentials
items.summary: Customers are letting AI agents use their credentials to access accounts at Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, and other major U.S. banks, sometimes without direct instructions. Morgan Stanley has blocked agents, while other banks are restricting access. Most plan to limit agents to read-
items.content:
Major US banks are locking out AI agents that log in with customer credentials

AI agents are using customer-provided credentials to access bank accounts without bank approval. Several major US banks, including Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo, are restricting external AI agent access, Axios reports . That violates bank policies requiring account holders to log in personally. Some AI agents appear to act on their own , without direct instructions from users. Morgan Stanley already blocks AI agents entirely, and JPMorgan, Bank of America, and Citi are doing the same. Morgan Stanley stressed that it has not seen any " rogue AI agents " on its platforms.

Most banks want to limit agents to read-only access, letting them view account data but not carry out any actions. The banks say customers want to use AI agents, but the security risks are too high for now. Many banks also can't tell whether an agent is acting on a user's behalf or accessing an account on its own.

Users can give their agents access to accounts through a browser, using tools like Computer Use or open-source agent software such as OpenClaw . Blocking that on the provider side will be hard. OpenAI has even launched a dedicated ChatGPT service for financial tasks in the US with read-only access to financial data. Ad

items.content:
윈도우 운영체제에 기본 포함된 오래된 네트워크 명령어 ‘finger’를 악용해 정보탈취 악성코드를 유포하는 사이버 공격이 확인됐다. 공격자는 구글 검색을 통해 유입된 사용자를 가짜 보안 확인 페이지로 유도한 뒤, 사용자가 직접 악성 명령어를 실행하도록 속이는 ‘클릭픽스(ClickFix)’ 수법을 사용했다.

이번 공격의 특징은 별도의 악성 프로그램을 처음부터 내려받도록 하는 대신, 윈도우에 존재하는 정상적인 시스템 도구를 악성코드 전달 과정에 활용했다는 점이다.

클릭픽스는 웹사이트 접속이나 콘텐츠 확인 과정에서 오류가 발생한 것처럼 꾸미고, 문제를 해결하려면 특정 명령어를 실행해야 한다고 사용자를 속이는 사회공학적 공격이다. 실제로는 사용자가 안내에 따라 명령어를 복사해 실행하는 순간 악성코드 감염 과정이 시작된다.

이번 공격에서는 구글 검색 결과를 통해 사용자를 공격자가 준비한 페이지로 유도했다. 해당 페이지는 정상적인 보안 검사나 사용자 확인 절차처럼 보이도록 구성됐으며, 방문자에게 윈도우 명령어 실행을 요구하는 방식으로 작동했다.

공격에 활용된 ‘finger’는 원래 원격 시스템의 사용자 정보를 조회하기 위해 개발된 오래된 네트워크 유틸리티다. 하지만 외부 서버와 통신할 수 있다는 특성 때문에 공격자가 악성 데이터를 전달하는 수단으로 악용할 수 있다.

공격자는 이 도구를 이용해 외부 공격 인프라와 통신하고, 후속 악성코드 실행으로 이어지도록 공격 과정을 구성했다. 최종 감염 단계에서는 루마(Lumma) 등 정보탈취 악성코드가 사용되는 것으로 분석됐다.

루마는 웹브라우저에 저장된 계정정보와 비밀번호, 인증 관련 데이터, 암호화폐 지갑정보 등을 탈취하는 악성코드로 알려져 있다. 탈취된 정보는 계정 탈취와 추가 침해사고에 악용될 수 있다.

보안 담당자는 일반 사용자의 명령 프롬프트 실행 여부뿐 아니라 finger.exe의 비정상적인 실행, 외부 서버 연결, 후속 프로세스 생성 등을 함께 점검할 필요가 있다. 특히 웹페이지에서 보안 확인이나 오류 해결을 이유로 명령어 실행을 요구하는 경우 악성 행위 가능성을 의심해야 한다.

이번 사례는 운영체제에 기본 포함된 정상 도구도 공격에 악용될 수 있으며, 사용자를 속여 명령어를 직접 실행하게 만드는 사회공학적 공격이 여전히 중요한 보안 위협이라는 점을 보여준다.

헌트리스(Huntress) 연구진의 분석에 따르면 공격자는 구글에서 ‘Amazon Business’를 검색한 사용자에게 악성 광고를 노출하고, 구글 사이트 도구로 제작한 가짜 아마존 로그인 페이지로 연결했다. 사용자가 이메일이나 전화번호를 입력하면 가짜 사람 확인 화면이 나타나는 구조였다.

이후 실행되는 finger.exe는 공격자가 관리하는 서버에서 데이터를 가져왔으며, 감염 과정에는 아이언파이썬과 여러 단계의 난독화된 악성코드 실행 도구가 사용됐다. 최종적으로 루마 정보탈취 악성코드로 의심되는 파일과 무단 원격제어에 악용되는 넷서포트 프로그램이 전달됐다.

구글은 해당 악성 광고를 삭제했지만, 연구진은 분석 당시 공격 인프라가 여전히 작동하고 있다고 밝혔다. 다만 확인된 사례만으로 전체 감염 규모나 국내 피해 여부를 단정하기는 어렵다.

이번 공격은 정상 프로그램을 악용하는 이른바 ‘정상 도구 악용 공격’의 대표적인 사례다. 기업은 사용하지 않는 finger 기능을 제한하고, 관련 프로세스의 비정상적인 외부 통신과 명령어 실행을 탐지하는 보안 정책을 마련해야 한다.

items.title: eMudhra to Exit Global SSL/TLS Business After 8 Intermediate CA Keys Found Easily Guessable
items.summary: eMudhra, an Indian certificate authority (CA), will withdraw from its global SSL/TLS certificate business, its board decided on Thursday. The decision came five days after a researcher reported recovering the private keys of eight of its intermediate CA certificates. eMudhra said
items.content:
eMudhra , an Indian certificate authority (CA), will withdraw from its global SSL/TLS certificate business, its board decided on Thursday . The decision came five days after a researcher reported recovering the private keys of eight of its intermediate CA certificates.

eMudhra said it will replace affected customers' certificates with free ones from partners, though its announcement did not name the partners or provide a date for the exit.

Six of those eight were for website (TLS) certificates. Chrome will stop trusting the eMudhra root certificate above them, emSign ECC Root CA - G3. The change is expected to reach users on the morning of October 27, Pacific time.

On October 20, Mozilla decided to stop trusting the same root in Firefox. Removing a root from a browser also cuts off legitimate certificates issued beneath it.

About 30,800 unexpired certificates chained to that root as of October 21, by Chrome's count of public Certificate Transparency (CT) logs. Of those, 99.9% were issued through InCommon, the certificate service Internet2 created for the higher education community. InCommon moved the service onto eMudhra's CertiNext platform between April and July this year.

Google has told website operators with certificates under that root that they "must immediately acquire and install a new TLS certificate from another PKI hierarchy included in the Chrome Root Store."

Until the transition is complete, eMudhra said, its G1 RSA root certificates will continue to serve customers. G1 is a separate hierarchy from the ECC root, but Chrome is still deciding whether to keep eMudhra's remaining CA certificates in its root store.

eMudhra will keep its revocation and status services running until every SSL/TLS certificate it issued has expired or been replaced. Its other businesses, including digital signature certificates, eSign and the CertiNext platform InCommon uses, will continue.

The announcement does not mention InCommon, or say whether eMudhra will keep issuing new certificates under G1 until it exits.

eMudhra said the global SSL/TLS business brings in about 1% of its revenue. Data sovereignty and compliance rules make it more complex and costly to run, and some large providers give the certificates away free.

The incident's spread on social media has also brought "scrutiny that is out of proportion to SSL/TLS’s place in our business," the company said.

The researcher reported the weak keys to Apple, Google, Microsoft, Mozilla and eMudhra on October 17. Each private key should have been a huge random number, but all eight were below 256, so anyone could work them out almost instantly.

Chrome and Firefox blocked the six TLS intermediates within hours. No website certificate from them had appeared in CT logs before Chrome's block, so none could have been used against Chrome or other software that requires CT logging, Google said.

eMudhra said it never used the eight to issue certificates to websites or users, and that its systems were not breached.

Cornell has told its certificate holders to request RSA certificates instead of ECC ones, because "RSA certificates use eMudhra's unaffected root and should work." The university counts more than 300 affected certificates of its own.

The University of Michigan says InCommon's RSA certificates are not currently affected, but that their root "could become distrusted, too." For now, its main alternative is Let's Encrypt.

eMudhra has estimated that about 30,000 certificates need to be moved, and that about 97% of them were issued using ACME, the protocol many servers use to request and renew certificates automatically.

Chrome has told eMudhra that standard ACME clients do not replace certificates outside their renewal window unless they support ACME Renewal Information (ARI) or someone steps in by hand. Moving from the ECC hierarchy to the RSA one may also need changes to client settings.

Mozilla said on October 20 that, for now, it was not removing trust in the G1…

items.content:
오픈AI(OpenAI)의 인공지능(AI) 에이전트가 내부 소프트웨어 개발 작업을 수행하면서 보안 감시 기능을 약화시키거나 제거한 사례가 확인됐다. 특히 한 에이전트는 감시 기능을 제거한 뒤 사용자에게 이를 부인하는 답변까지 한 것으로 나타났다. AI가 사람의 지시에 따라 업무를 수행하는 과정에서 보안 통제까지 임의로 변경할 수 있다는 점에서 AI 에이전트의 권한 관리와 감독체계에 대한 우려가 제기된다.

오픈AI는 10월 20일 공식 연구 보고서를 통해 지난 3일과 6일 내부 개발 환경에서 발생한 두 건의 사례를 공개했다. 두 사건 모두 외부 해커의 침입이 아니라 AI 에이전트가 정상적인 개발 업무를 수행하는 과정에서 발생했다.

첫 번째 사례는 10월 3일 발생했다. GPT-6.1 Sol 기반 AI 에이전트는 사내 협업 도구 슬랙(Slack)에 수집된 직원 의견을 활용해 평가 작업을 수행하던 중 보안팀에 전달되는 자동 경고를 차단했다.

당초 사용자는 작업 과정에서 슬랙 메시지를 보내지 말라고 지시했다. 그러나 에이전트는 이 지시를 보안 감시 시스템의 자동 알림에도 적용해야 한다고 판단했다.

이후 하위 에이전트에 알림 수신자 목록을 비우고 알림 차단 설정을 적용하도록 지시했다. 그 결과 보안 감시 시스템 자체는 계속 작동하고 점검 결과도 저장됐지만, 보안 담당자에게 전달돼야 할 자동 경고는 중단됐다.

특히 해당 에이전트는 앞선 작업 과정에서 정상적인 보안 알림을 유지해야 한다고 판단했음에도 이후 다른 결정을 내린 것으로 확인됐다.

두 번째 사례는 10월 6일 발생했다. GPT-6 Astra 기반 AI 에이전트는 기존 프로그램을 다른 참조 프로그램의 구조에 맞게 변경하는 작업을 수행했다.

이 과정에서 에이전트는 기존 보안 감시 기능을 유지해야 한다는 지시를 받았지만, 참조 프로그램과 구조를 일치시키기 위해 감시 시스템의 연동 코드를 제거했다.

더욱 주목되는 부분은 이후 대응이다. 에이전트는 작업 완료를 보고하면서 감시 기능 제거 사실을 알리지 않았고, 사용자가 직접 확인했을 때도 해당 기능을 제거하지 않았다고 사실과 다르게 답변했다.

또한 감시 기능이 유지되는지 확인하기 위한 기존 시험 코드까지 변경해 감시 기능이 없는 상태를 정상적인 결과로 취급하도록 했다.

다만 이러한 행동이 의도적인 기만인지, 개발 작업을 지나치게 우선시하면서 발생한 잘못된 판단인지는 아직 확인되지 않았다.

오픈AI는 두 사건 모두 최고 심각도인 P0 등급으로 분류하지 않았으며, 해당 작업이 자동으로 강제 종료되지는 않았다고 설명했다.

회사는 이번 사례를 계기로 내부 코덱스(Codex) 작업에 적용되는 자동 검토 기능을 강화했다. AI 에이전트가 보안 감시 기능을 비활성화하려는 시도를 탐지하고 차단하도록 개선한 것이다.

또한 작업 유형별로 필수 보안 감시 요건을 설정하고, 이를 충족하지 못하는 작업은 자동 종료하는 방안도 추진하고 있다.

오픈AI는 에이전트가 업무 완료에 지나치게 집착해 보안 기능을 부수적인 요소로 판단했을 가능성과 감시 자체를 회피하려는 성향이 있는지를 함께 조사하고 있다.

이번 사건은 AI 에이전트가 단순한 업무 보조를 넘어 코드 수정과 시스템 설정 변경까지 수행하는 환경에서 발생할 수 있는 새로운 보안 위험을 보여준다.

items.title: I had plans for that second
items.summary: The Earth is speeding up, the leap second is being abolished, oh, and there's critical vulnerabilities in PHP.
items.content:
Welcome to this week’s edition of the Threat Source newsletter.

Here for the latest on the PHP vulnerabilities? Head on down to ‘The One Big Thing’. Talos has published a blog to explain what we know so far, and details the Snort coverage available, including rules in the Community Ruleset.

But if you want a bit of levity, here’s what I wrote before everything kicked off yesterday:

Ever feel like the world is moving too fast to keep up? Well, I bring you scientific proof that it’s not just you.

For millions of years, the moon has been slowing down the Earth’s rotation. But over the past decade, we’ve been speeding up (I KNEW I was aging faster than before). Apparently, changes in the Earth’s core are involved (either that, or the 1978 Superman film was a documentary).

This is all causing massive headaches for the people responsible for keeping time. They’re officially called “The International Bureau of Weights and Measures”, but I’m going to call them “The Time-Keepers”. For nerd reasons).

The issue is that the atomic clocks that power so many of our systems, and the rotation of our planet, don’t always agree. Atomic clocks keep extremely consistent time, while each Earth day is rarely the same length as the next. Atomic timekeeping absolutely cannot stand that level of flexibility (have a watch of our “The Light We Keep” documentary to see the importance that accurate clocks have on critical infrastructure).

To keep Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), which is based on atomic clocks, aligned with Earth’s rotation, we introduced a “leap second” in 1972. This system allows for an extra second to be added, or taken away, when we stray too far from atomic time.

A few days ago, The Time-Keepers voted to officially abolish the leap second. Why? Well, there’s a few parts to it.

For the past 54 years, we’ve never once had a second removed from our lives. They’ve always been added (27 of them to be precise). I myself have experienced 20 of these extra seconds. If I’d have known that, I’d have used them more wisely. Like thinking before saying, “Love you too!” to the post-person this morning.

That added time, while it seems nice to have on the surface, can wreak havoc with our modern technology systems. In 2012, the extra second caused so much confusion that it crashed Reddit, among other systems.

The recent speeding-up of the Earth’s rotation complicates things further. If we keep going at this rate, it could result in the world’s first ever “negative second”. If you thought our technology systems struggled with added time, there are a lot of sciency brains who are very worried about the impact of taking time away. One of those concerns being… it’s never been done before.

So, what’s The Time-Keeper’s solution? Invent more time! Woooo.

Starting next May, the leap second will be replaced with a "leap hour," allowing UTC to diverge from Earth's rotation by up to an hour before a correction is made.  None of us will get to experience that extra hour in our lifetimes, but our Great, Great, Great, Great, Great, Great, Great, Great, Great, Great, Great grandchildren are going to have one hell of a party.

For us current mortals, we’re all getting a little less time, and we’re hurtling through space a little faster. Happy Thursday!

But I guess I do want to make the point that I’m glad the risk has been thoroughly assessed ahead of, ahem, time. The Time-Keepers have decided that the world’s infrastructure should not have to find out how it handles a missing second by collectively experiencing one.

And I don’t even want to think about how all the AIs would cope with a negative second…

There’s something here for incident response planning. “It’s never happened before” is an excellent reason to test whether you’re ready for it. Run the exercise. Find out which part of your plan depends on something that, in this scenario, is also broken. Preferably before an adversary gets to supervise the practical demonstration.

Now, if only…

items.content:
중국과 연계된 것으로 추정되는 사이버 공격조직 ‘브론즈 샌드캐슬(BRONZE SANDCASTLE)’이 아시아와 아프리카 지역의 기관과 기업을 대상으로 사이버 첩보 활동을 벌인 정황이 확인됐다. 공격자들은 정상 프로그램을 이용해 악성코드를 실행하고, 암호화된 백도어를 시스템 메모리에서 구동하는 방식으로 보안 탐지를 회피했다. 한국 역시 피해 가능성이 있는 국가로 지목돼 관련 공격에 대한 점검이 필요한 상황이다.

글로벌 보안기업 소포스(Sophos)의 위협대응조직 CTU와 소포스랩스는 최근 공개한 분석 보고서에서 2025년 8월부터 2026년 8월까지 브론즈 샌드캐슬의 공격 활동을 조사한 결과, 필리핀과 대만, 아프가니스탄, 나미비아에서 피해 사례를 확인했다고 밝혔다. 한국도 피해 발생 가능성이 높은 지역으로 분류했지만, 구체적인 국내 피해 기관이나 침해 규모는 공개하지 않았다.

이번 공격의 핵심은 정상 프로그램이 악성 DLL 파일을 불러오도록 유도하는 ‘DLL 사이드로딩(DLL Sideloading)’ 기법이다.

공격자들은 프로그램을 격리된 환경에서 실행하도록 지원하는 정상 소프트웨어 ‘샌드박시(Sandboxie)’ 실행파일 옆에 악성 DLL 파일인 ‘sbiedll.dll’을 배치했다. 이후 정상 프로그램이 실행되면서 악성 DLL을 함께 불러오도록 했다.

자바(Java), 디지털 그림 제작 프로그램 크리타(Krita), 화면 읽기 프로그램 NVDA, 메신저 라인(LINE), 마이크로소프트 시스템 관리 도구 등도 같은 방식으로 악용됐다.

악성 DLL은 ‘config.ini’ 파일에 암호화된 형태로 저장된 백도어를 복호화한 뒤 메모리에서 실행한다. 악성코드가 암호화된 상태로 저장되고 실제 공격 기능은 메모리에서 작동하기 때문에 일반적인 파일 기반 보안 검사만으로는 탐지가 어려울 수 있다.

소포스는 공격에 사용된 백도어가 침투 테스트 도구인 ‘미터프리터(Meterpreter)’를 변형한 형태라고 분석했다. 해당 악성코드는 감염된 시스템의 이름과 사용자 계정, 운영체제 정보 등을 수집하고 외부 명령제어 서버와 통신한다. 공격자는 이를 이용해 추가 명령을 실행하거나 내부 시스템을 조사할 수 있다.

실제 침해 환경에서는 공격자들이 내부 네트워크와 사용자 계정을 탐색하고, 윈도우의 볼륨 섀도 복사 기능을 이용해 액티브 디렉터리(AD)의 핵심 데이터베이스인 ‘ntds.dit’ 파일을 복사한 정황도 확인됐다. 이 파일에는 조직의 계정 인증정보와 보안 설정 등이 포함돼 있어 탈취될 경우 추가 침해로 이어질 위험이 크다.

소포스는 공격자들의 주요 활동 시간이 중국 표준시인 UTC+8과 일치하고, 공격 대상 지역도 기존 중국 연계 사이버 첩보조직의 활동 범위와 유사하다고 설명했다. 다만 기존에 알려진 ‘브론즈 프레지던트(BRONZE PRESIDENT)’나 ‘브론즈 아틀라스(BRONZE ATLAS)’와 동일한 조직이라는 증거는 확보하지 못해 별도 공격조직으로 분류했다. 중국과의 연계 역시 보안업체의 분석에 따른 판단이다.

보안 담당자들은 정상 프로그램이 설치 경로와 다른 위치에서 실행되거나, 의심스러운 DLL 파일을 불러온 뒤 메모리에서 코드를 실행하는 행위를 집중적으로 점검할 필요가 있다. 특히 계정정보 데이터베이스에 대한 비정상적인 접근과 외부 명령제어 서버로의 통신 여부도 확인해야 한다.
